7.name: Disk Error
solutions: Run CHKDSK
Check SMART status
Replace disk if necessary

11.name: Disk controller error
11.cause: The driver detected a controller error on a disk
solutions: Check cables and the controller
Check SMART status
Update storage controller driver and firmware

15.name: Disk not ready
15.cause: A disk was not ready for access
solutions: Check cables, power and the enclosure
Check SMART status

17.name: Corrected PCI Express error (WHEA)
17.cause: A PCI Express device reported an error that the hardware corrected
solutions: Check the device named in the event
Update device drivers and firmware
Reseat the card if the error repeats

18.name: Fatal hardware error (WHEA)
18.cause: The hardware reported a fatal error through Windows Hardware Error Architecture
solutions: Open the event details to see the failing component
Run vendor hardware diagnostics
Check CPU, memory and PCIe devices; update firmware

19.name: Corrected hardware error (WHEA)
19.cause: The hardware reported an error that it corrected
solutions: Open the event details to see the component
Check cooling and power
Update BIOS/firmware if the error repeats

19.name: Windows Update Successful Installation
solutions: No action required

20.name: Windows Update Installation Failure
solutions: Review Windows Update logs
Run Windows Update Troubleshooter
Check Microsoft Store application status
Close running applications and retry update

36.name: Shadow copies aborted
36.cause: Shadow copies were aborted because the storage area could not grow
solutions: Free space on the volume
Increase or move the shadow copy storage area
Review backup schedules

36.name: Time service stopped advertising as good time source
36.cause: The Windows Time service lost its reliable time source
solutions: Check the configured time source
Check network access to the time server
Run w32tm /query /status

37.name: Processor speed limited by firmware
37.cause: The CPU is being slowed by firmware, usually because of heat or a power limit
solutions: Check cooling, fans and dust
Check power plan and power supply capacity
Update BIOS/firmware

41.name: Unexpected restart (Kernel-Power)
solutions: Open the event and read BugcheckCode. If it is not 0, the PC crashed with a blue screen: convert the decimal number to hex (for example 159 = 0x9F) and look up that stop code; also check Event 1001 nearby.
If PowerButtonTimestamp is not 0, someone forced the power off with the power button (usually because the PC was frozen).
If every value is 0, suspect power: unplugged or drained battery, power cut, faulty or weak power supply, or a hard hang.
Check what changed just before: drivers, updates or new services (Event 7045) installed shortly before the first restart.
Check CPU/GPU temperatures and test RAM if restarts keep happening with no stop code.

43.name: Windows Update Started
solutions: No action required

44.name: Windows Update Installation Started
solutions: No action required

46.name: Crash dump initialization failed
46.cause: Windows could not prepare to write a memory dump if the system crashes
solutions: Check the paging file size and the system drive free space
Check the crash dump settings

51.name: Disk error during paging
51.cause: An error occurred on a disk while reading or writing virtual memory
solutions: Check SMART status
Run CHKDSK
Check cables and the controller

52.name: Disk predicts failure
52.cause: The disk reported that it expects to fail (SMART)
solutions: Back up critical data immediately
Replace the disk as soon as possible

55.name: NTFS Corruption
solutions: Run CHKDSK /F
Verify disk health

104.name: Event log cleared
solutions: Confirm the clearing was authorized
Check who cleared it and when

129.name: Storage device reset
129.cause: Windows had to reset a storage device because it did not respond
solutions: Check SMART status and device firmware
Update storage controller driver
Check cables, power and drive health

129.name: Time service: domain peer unavailable
129.cause: The time client could not select a domain time source
solutions: Check connectivity to the domain controller
Check DNS
Run w32tm /resync

134.name: Time service: manual peer unavailable
134.cause: The time client could not use the configured time server
solutions: Check DNS resolution of the time server name
Check network access to the time server

153.name: Disk I/O retried
153.cause: A disk input/output operation had to be retried
solutions: Check SMART status
Check cables, backplane and controller
Update storage driver and firmware

154.name: Disk I/O failed (hardware error)
154.cause: A disk input/output operation failed because of a hardware error
solutions: Back up data
Check SMART status
Check cables and the controller; replace the disk if errors continue

157.name: Disk removed unexpectedly
157.cause: A disk was removed without being ejected first
solutions: Check cables, the enclosure and power
Check the storage controller

161.name: Crash dump creation failed
161.cause: Windows could not create a memory dump after a crash
solutions: Check the paging file size and free space on the system drive
Check the crash dump settings

219.name: Driver failed to load for a device
219.cause: Windows could not load a driver for a device
solutions: Identify the device and driver in the event
Update or reinstall the driver
Check Device Manager for the device

1001.name: System crash (bugcheck) recorded
1001.cause: The computer restarted after a stop error (blue screen)
solutions: Note the bugcheck code in the event data and look it up
Update or roll back recently installed drivers and updates
Analyze the memory dump with WinDbg
Run memory diagnostics if the code points to memory

1001.name: Windows Error Reporting record
1001.cause: Windows recorded details of a program problem
solutions: Read the event data for the program and the error
Look for a matching Application Error (1000) event

1014.name: DNS name resolution timed out
1014.cause: None of the configured DNS servers answered in time
solutions: Check the DNS server addresses on the adapter
Test connectivity to the DNS servers
Check the network link and firewall

1030.name: Group Policy: could not query policy objects
1030.cause: Windows could not read the list of Group Policy objects
solutions: Read the previous Group Policy events for the cause
Check DNS, time and domain controller reachability

1058.name: Group Policy: could not read policy file
1058.cause: Windows could not read a Group Policy file from SYSVOL
solutions: Check that SYSVOL is reachable from this computer
Check DNS, DFS and permissions on SYSVOL

1074.name: Planned shutdown or restart
1074.cause: A user or process started a shutdown or restart
solutions: Check the reason and the process or user named in the event if it was not expected

1129.name: Group Policy: no domain controller connection
1129.cause: Group Policy could not be processed because the domain controller was not reachable
solutions: Check network connectivity and DNS
Check that the computer can reach a domain controller
Run gpupdate /force after fixing connectivity

2013.name: Disk at or near capacity
solutions: Free space on the drive named in the event
Move or archive old data
Extend the volume

4101.name: Display driver stopped responding and recovered
4101.cause: The graphics driver stopped responding and Windows reset it
solutions: Update the graphics driver
Check GPU temperature and power
Check for faulty monitors or cables if it repeats

4199.name: IP address conflict
4199.cause: Another device on the network uses the same IP address
solutions: Find the device with the conflicting address (MAC address is in the event)
Check DHCP scope and static address assignments

5719.name: Netlogon: no domain controller available
5719.cause: The computer could not set up a secure session with a domain controller
solutions: Check network connectivity and DNS
Check that a domain controller is reachable
Check that the computer account is valid

5805.name: Netlogon: machine session setup failed
5805.cause: A computer failed to authenticate to the domain
solutions: Check that the computer account exists and is enabled
Reset the machine secure channel if needed
Check time synchronization

6005.name: Event Log service started
6005.cause: The Event Log service started, which normally happens at boot
solutions: No action needed; use it as a boot time marker

6006.name: Event Log service stopped
6006.cause: The Event Log service stopped, which normally happens at a clean shutdown
solutions: No action needed; a missing 6006 before a boot suggests an unclean shutdown

6008.name: Previous shutdown was unexpected
6008.cause: System was not properly shut down
solutions: Look at the same time for Event 41 (Kernel-Power) and Event 1001 (blue screen): 1001 means a crash; 41 with no 1001 usually means power loss or a forced power-off.
Event 1074 just before means someone or something restarted it on purpose, so this is not a fault.
If it repeats: check the power supply/UPS and mains, then drivers and hardware (RAM, disk).

6013.name: System uptime
6013.cause: Daily report of how long the system has been running
solutions: No action needed

7000.name: Service failed to start
solutions: Read the reason in the event text; it names the cause.

"Did not respond in a timely fashion": the service was too slow to start. Check load at boot; as a workaround raise ServicesPipeTimeout (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control, DWORD in milliseconds; default 30000) a little at a time, then restart.
"Logon failure": the service account's password changed or it lacks the 'Log on as a service' right (check secpol.msc and Group Policy).
"The system cannot find the file specified" or "Access is denied": the service program is missing, renamed or blocked; repair the application and check file permissions.
Check events from the service's own provider and the Application log at the same time.

7001.name: Service dependency failed
7001.cause: A service could not start because a service it depends on failed
solutions: Fix the service it depends on first
Check dependencies in the service's properties

7009.name: Service start timeout
7009.cause: A service did not respond to the start request in time
solutions: Check the system for heavy load at boot
Review the service and its dependencies
Check events from the service's own provider

7011.name: Service request timeout
7011.cause: A service did not reply to a control request in time
solutions: Check the service for hangs or high load
Check events from the service's own provider

7022.name: Service hung on starting
7022.cause: A service started but never finished starting
solutions: Check the service and its dependencies
Review events from the service's own provider

7023.name: Service terminated with an error
7023.cause: A service stopped because of an error
solutions: Read the error in the event text
Check events from the service's own provider

7024.name: Service terminated with a service-specific error
7024.cause: A service stopped with an error code specific to that service
solutions: Read the error code in the event text
Check the product documentation for that service

7026.name: Boot or system driver failed to load
7026.cause: A driver needed at startup could not be loaded
solutions: Identify the driver in the event text
Reinstall or roll back the driver
Run sfc /scannow if system files may be damaged

7031.name: Service crashed (recovery action taken)
7031.cause: A service ended unexpectedly and Windows is taking the configured recovery action
solutions: Identify the service in the event text
Check the Application log and the service's own logs
Review the service's recovery settings

7034.name: Service terminated unexpectedly
solutions: Identify the service in the event text
Check the Application log and the service's own logs

7036.name: Service state change
7036.cause: A service entered the running or stopped state
solutions: No action needed unless the change was not expected

7038.name: Service logon failed
7038.cause: A service could not log on with its configured account
solutions: Check the service account name and password
Check that the account is not locked or expired

7040.name: Service Configuration Change
7040.cause: A Windows service startup type was modified
solutions: Verify the service change is expected
Review recent software installations
Check service dependencies

7045.name: New service installed
7045.cause: A new service was installed on the system
solutions: Confirm the installation was expected
Check the service name and file path for anything unfamiliar

10010.name: DCOM server did not register
10010.cause: A DCOM server did not register in the required time
solutions: Check the application or service that owns the CLSID in the event
Repair or reinstall that application if it repeats

10016.name: DCOM permission warning (normally harmless)
10016.cause: A Windows component asked for a DCOM permission it does not have. Microsoft documents this as expected, by-design behavior: the code retries with other parameters and succeeds
solutions: Usually nothing to do: Microsoft says these events can be safely ignored.
Do not change DCOM permissions just to silence it; Microsoft does not recommend that and it can cause side effects.
Investigate only if an application or service fails at the same time; the APPID and CLSID in the event identify the component.
To hide them from view, filter them out in Event Viewer (or use --exclude-event-ids 10016 in this tool).

36874.name: TLS: no common cipher suite
36874.cause: A client could not agree on a cipher suite with this server
solutions: Identify the client that is connecting
Review the TLS and cipher settings on the server
Update the client if it is outdated

36887.name: TLS: fatal alert received
36887.cause: The remote side ended a TLS connection with a fatal alert
solutions: Check the alert code in the event
Check certificates and TLS settings on both sides

36888.name: TLS: fatal alert sent
36888.cause: This computer ended a TLS connection with a fatal alert
solutions: Check the alert code in the event
Check certificates and TLS settings on both sides

4625.name: Failed logon
4625.cause: An account failed to log on (wrong password, unknown user, locked or disabled account)
solutions: Check the account name and the source address in the event data
Look for many failures from one source (password guessing)
Check for services or scheduled tasks using an old password

4740.name: Account locked out
4740.cause: An account was locked out after too many failed logons
solutions: Find the computer causing the failed logons (caller computer in the event data)
Check for old saved passwords, mapped drives and services
Unlock the account after fixing the cause

4720.name: User account created
4720.cause: A new user account was created
solutions: Confirm the account was created by an authorized administrator
Check which groups it was added to

4722.name: User account enabled
solutions: Confirm the account was enabled on purpose

4724.name: Password reset attempted
4724.cause: An administrator or process tried to reset an account password
solutions: Confirm the reset was authorized
Check who performed it (subject in the event data)

4725.name: User account disabled
solutions: Confirm the account was disabled on purpose

4726.name: User account deleted
solutions: Confirm the deletion was authorized

4728.name: Member added to a global security group
4728.cause: An account was added to a security-enabled global group
solutions: Confirm the change was authorized, especially for privileged groups

4732.name: Member added to a local security group
4732.cause: An account was added to a security-enabled local group (for example Administrators)
solutions: Confirm the change was authorized, especially for the Administrators group
Check who made the change

4756.name: Member added to a universal security group
4756.cause: An account was added to a security-enabled universal group
solutions: Confirm the change was authorized, especially for privileged groups

4719.name: Audit policy changed
4719.cause: The system audit policy was changed
solutions: Confirm the change was authorized
Check who changed it and what was changed

4697.name: Service installed in the system
4697.cause: A service was installed on the system
solutions: Confirm the service is expected
Check the service file path for anything unfamiliar

4698.name: Scheduled task created
solutions: Confirm the task is expected
Check the program the task runs

4771.name: Kerberos pre-authentication failed
4771.cause: A Kerberos ticket request failed, usually a wrong password
solutions: Check the account and the client address in the event data
Look for many failures from one source

1102.name: Audit log cleared
1102.cause: The Security audit log was cleared
solutions: Confirm the clearing was authorized
Check who cleared it (subject in the event data)
Review other events around this time

1000.name: Application crash
1000.cause: A program crashed (faulting application and module are in the event data)
solutions: Note the faulting application and module in the event data
Update or reinstall the program
Check for a recent update or a new driver

1002.name: Application hang
solutions: Note the program in the event data
Update or reinstall the program
Check disk and memory load at that time

1026.name: .NET Runtime error
1026.cause: A .NET application had an unhandled exception
solutions: Read the exception text in the event message
Update or reinstall the application
Check that the required .NET version is installed

11708.name: Installation failed
11708.cause: A Windows Installer package failed to install
solutions: Check the product named in the event
Run the installer again as administrator
Check free disk space and the installer log

8193.name: Volume Shadow Copy error
8193.cause: The Volume Shadow Copy Service reported an error
solutions: Read the error code in the event
Check the VSS service and the writers (vssadmin list writers)
Check free space on the volume

2004.name: Low virtual memory
2004.cause: Windows detected that it was running out of virtual memory
solutions: Check which programs use the most memory (listed in the event)
Close or fix the memory-hungry program
Add memory or increase the page file

33.name: Side-by-side configuration error
33.cause: A program could not load because of a missing or wrong component
solutions: Reinstall the program or its Visual C++ runtime
Check the component named in the event
